changelog: The System Health screen's network check now reports two things: whether the Ethernet port has a connection, and whether this system can actually reach the internet -- including which connection is carrying the traffic when it is not the cable.
details: 50a (bench revision, stacked for a later fleet release together with the device-side script refresh): v48b's network row could report the Ethernet port's link only, so a unit whose cable was unplugged -- or whose port was dead, the customer case behind v48b -- showed a warning and nothing else while the system was in fact still online. cytech_check_eth.sh now makes a second, independent measurement: an outbound TCP connect() probe to well-known public anycast endpoints (1.1.1.1:443, 8.8.8.8:53, 9.9.9.9:443, 223.5.5.5:443, first answer wins), addressed by IP only so a DNS failure can never read as 'no internet'. The probe runs twice: first source-bound to the port's own IPv4 -- a success means the port's address carried the traffic, so net='port' -- and, if that fails, once unbound, where a success means the system is online through some other connection (net='other'). For 'other', net_via names the interface the successful connect() actually left from (found by matching the socket's local address against /sys/class/net), with wl* rendered as 'Wi-Fi' and usb*/enx* as 'a USB network adapter'. Neither succeeds -> net='none'. The result file gains net, net_via and net_message alongside ts/status/message; sensor.cytech_ethernet_result exposes net and net_message as attributes under the SAME unique_id (no new entity), and dashboards/system.yaml renders one badge per fact. The port line keeps its OK and NO_IFACE wording; its NO_LINK text drops the 'online via X' sentence, which the internet line now says more accurately (link is not reachability) -- and, in the other direction, a port that has a link while nothing is reachable now produces the message that the problem is further along the network, which is the distinction this revision exists for. Still display-only: no email, no popup, no alert kind. Offline-test-only env overrides (CY_ETH_DEV, CY_ETH_CARRIER, CY_ETH_IP, CY_NET_TARGETS) make every branch reproducible without unplugging anything; all remain strictly read-only, as before. Bench-verified 2026-09-22 on cytech.local from the served bytes: the check offered 50a, the update landed all three files md5-identical to the tag blobs, Core restarted (packages changed), the boot automation ran the new script and wrote the new result schema, the dashboard template taken from the shipped YAML rendered both badges and rendered an old-schema result file without a stray badge, and all seven status/reachability branches were exercised live through the read-only overrides (0-6 s each) alongside 13 unit tests on the shipped python. Display-only reconfirmed: no alert email, no notification. Not published yet -- 50a is a bench revision and ships inside the next bare-number release.
